interpretation: Error is not monotonic with row count under TSPACK; knot locations interact with constitutive curvature.
60 rows is faster in this run but less accurate than 50 and 75 on the worst tested metrics, so row count alone is not a smooth fidelity control.
75 rows materially improves worst head error relative to 50, but its worst theta error is larger because the coarse profile dominates.
100 rows provides the strongest overall fidelity of these practical candidates while retaining substantial serialized acceleration.
50 remains attractive when modest bounded constitutive error is acceptable; 100 is the conservative practical candidate.
decision: Do not declare a universal row-count optimum from these fixtures. Carry 50 and 100 as two purpose points; optionally 75 for diagnostic knot-placement research, not as default.
